period: second temple period (N-S tombs); last few centuries (E-W tombs)
quote: As a result of Reeder's mapping, we were able to locate 1178 tombs.
notes: One single cemetery on the same plateau as the ruins, spreading east over four hills (North Hill; North, Middle, South Fingers) (p.135 n.1). 1178 tombs mapped (p.141); more than 1138 tombs (p.142); Table II (p.143): 999 N-S, 54 E-W, 124 GPR-only, total 1177. Most tombs marked by a covering of stones oriented N-S (p.137). Skeletal remains at depth 0.8-2.5 m in both N-S and E-W tombs; E-W tombs generally shallower (p.150 n.55). NW corner covered 1998 by visitors' center extension; paved road and visitors' center built over parts (p.140; p.142 n.30). Maps 1-3 (pp.138-139) are illegible in the text copy; no positions keyed from them.

quote: 825 in the Western Section
notes: Cemetery section. Table II (p.143): 727 N-S, 3 E-W, 95 GPR-only, total 825. Also called 'Western Section' / 'Main Cemetery'. Total includes 39 GPR points near the ruins that may not be burials (p.142 n.32). De Vaux excavated 28 tombs here (p.137 n.8); at least 54 excavated tombs (p.141 n.21). Crossed by a 'division path' (p.141).

quote: we will call the northernmost of these hills the "North Hill,"
notes: Cemetery section. Table II (p.143): 58 N-S, 1 E-W, 22 GPR-only, total 81. Northernmost of the four hills (p.135 n.1). De Vaux tombs 9 and 10 here (p.137 n.8); two excavated tombs (n.21). Tombs buried by vehicle traffic; 22 located by GPR (p.142).

quote: "North Finger," "Middle Finger," and "South Finger"
notes: Cemetery section. Table II (p.143): 50 N-S, 1 E-W, 0 GPR-only, total 51. One of three hills south of the North Hill (p.135 n.1). No de Vaux tombs; five robbed tombs (n.21-22).

quote: 129 in the Middle Finger
notes: Cemetery section. Table II (p.143): 122 N-S, 6 E-W, 1 GPR-only, total 129. One de Vaux tomb; six excavated tombs (n.8, n.21). Square building (mourning enclosure) at its eastern extremity (p.147); zinc coffin tomb 978 in its eastern part (p.143).

quote: ninety-one in the South Finger
notes: Cemetery section. Table II (p.143): 42 N-S, 43 E-W, 6 GPR-only, total 91. Six de Vaux tombs; twelve excavated tombs (n.8, n.21). 43 E-W tombs (p.138 n.13).

quote: Further north, de Vaux found another burial ground with over a dozen tombs
notes: Lies further north than the main cemetery (no distance given); over a dozen tombs; not the North Hill; destroyed by military activity north of Khirbet Qumran, no longer identifiable (p.135 n.1). De Vaux tombs A and B here (p.137 n.8).

quote: small cemetery discovered south of Wadi Qumran ... all oriented east-west
notes: Small cemetery south of Wadi Qumran (de Vaux's 'Southern Cemetery'); all tombs long axis E-W; in all likelihood Bedouin burials (p.135 n.1).

quote: de Vaux's Tomb number 23 is indicated as being south of the division path
notes: Path dividing the cemetery (Humbert & Chambon map). Authors place de Vaux T23 (=Reeder 108?) north of it, H&C south of it (p.141, n.20 cont.).

quote: for a total building size of 4.50 x 5.05 m
notes: De Vaux's 'Point B' (dug 29 Nov 1951), re-excavated 2001, at the eastern edge of the Middle Finger, about 12 m east of burial 1001 and some 20 m short of the finger's eastern extremity (p.147, 152). W wall 4.50 m (N-S); SE corner 5.05 m from SW corner. One (possible) entrance in the N wall; opening_dirs N from 'in the north wall' (no direction stated otherwise). Walls c. 0.55 m wide of 0.20-0.30 m stones with light-coloured bonding agent between stones (mortar; plaster not mentioned). Floor destroyed; no benches found. Dated by c.140 second temple sherds. Plan Plate III (scale bar 0-2 m) not visible in the text copy.

quote: a western wall 4.50 m long and preserved in places up to three courses high
notes: Preserved up to three courses; width 'about 55 cm' stated for both walls; stones 20-30 cm; light-coloured bonding agent.

quote: a northern wall 3.80 m long of which only one course remained
notes: One course; leans outward towards the slope to the north (earthquake?). Entrance 1.80 m from NW corner, 0.60 m wide; wall continues E another 1.40 m before being cut off by the wadi north of the building (1.80+0.60+1.40=3.80).

quote: what seems to be the entrance to the building, 0.60 m wide
notes: In the north wall, 1.80 m from the NW corner; 'possible entrance' on Plate III; called 'our conjectured entrance' (p.150). Faces N because it is in the N wall.

quote: before being cut off by the wadi north of the building
notes: Wadi/slope immediately north of the Middle Finger building; it cuts off the N wall (p.147-148).

period: bones C14 170-40 BCE (1 sigma); reburial date open
quote: The pile was only 20 cm deep from the surface
notes: Map number 1000; 'not really a tomb' (n.33): pile of human bones of two women in secondary burial in the southern part of the building, opposite the conjectured entrance. Bones C14-dated to second temple period, but the reburial could be recent (n.56); authors think burial and building probably unrelated.
